newsitem.title: UK: French fail to pay UK lorry compensation - FTA.
newsitem.headline: French fail to pay UK lorry compensation - FTA.

text.p: The French government is failing to honour an agreement it made with the UK last December to compensate strike-affected British trucking firms, according to the UK's Freight Transport Association (FTA).
It said the agreement covered a fast track, compensation process for British companies that suffered losses as a result of French lorry driver strikes last November.

The FTA said it was unacceptable that three months on, entirely legitimate claims -- amounting to many thousands of pounds -- appeared nowhere near settlement, and the onus was now on the UK government to assure the scheme functioned as agreed.
The FTA said there was now the danger of the whole process being entangled in a web of bureaucracy caused by a deliberate policy of procrastination and obstruction in France.
The result was that UK businesses, many of them relatively small, were being denied vital compensation payments, it added.

The FTA estimated that on average, more than 1,000 British vehicles were blockaded in France on each of the 12 days that the blockade lasted. Many thousands more were forced to take diversions through neighbouring countries.
The association calculated the average daily cost of having a vehicle stranded was 180 to 250 stg, which did not include loss of goods or damaged vehicles or extra payments made to drivers.
